title: Ensure 4.5:1 contrast for syntax-highlighted code and keep code blocks when messages are already in the store
body:
> Comments in syntax-highlighted code have 4.36:1 color contrast in the Fluent theme, below the 4.5:1 required by WCAG 1.4.3 (axe `color-contrast`, serious).

## Changelog Entry

### Fixed

- Fixed syntax-highlighted code having less than 4.5:1 color contrast: comments in the light code block theme (`github-light-default`) were 4.36:1 in the Fluent theme and now use the muted text color of the theme, `#656d76` (5.03:1), in PR [#5893](https://github.com/microsoft/BotFramework-WebChat/pull/5893), by [@OEvgeny](https://github.com/OEvgeny)
- Fixed code blocks becoming empty when Web Chat is rendered with messages already in the store, such as again with the same store or from a saved state: code is shown without highlighting until the syntax highlighter is loaded, in PR [#5893](https://github.com/microsoft/BotFramework-WebChat/pull/5893), by [@OEvgeny](https://github.com/OEvgeny)

## Description

Web Chat paints the code block background itself. The Fluent theme uses `#fafafa` (light) and `#141414` (dark). The GitHub code themes were designed for `#ffffff` and `#0d1117`. On `#fafafa`, comments of `github-light-default` (`#6e7781`) are 4.36:1 by the WCAG formula, which axe rounds down to 4.35:1. The "View code" dialog of `side-by-side/codeblock.navigation.html` hit this, so that check was skipped.

The light code block theme passed to Shiki now replaces the comment color with `colorReplacements: { '#6e7781': '#656d76' }`. `#656d76` is the muted text color of the same theme (GitHub Primer's `fg.muted`), with about the same hue: 5.03:1 on `#fafafa` and 5.25:1 on `#ffffff`. The dark code block theme is unchanged.

The same Shiki integration also left code blocks empty when Web Chat was rendered with messages already in the store: rendered again with the same store, or with a store created from a saved state. These messages rendered before the new highlighter had loaded. `CodeHighlighterComposer` then called an `undefined` highlighter, and its error handler threw on `highlightCode.name`. The code block had already moved its code out, so it stayed empty. While no highlighter is set, `CodeHighlighterComposer` now uses the one above it, which is the plain-text highlighter by default.

## Design

- Only the failing color is replaced, statically, with Shiki's `colorReplacements` on the theme. Only comments fail: every other foreground of the two themes that JavaScript, Python, and TypeScript tokens use is at least 4.83:1 in the light theme (`#8250df` on `#fafafa`) and 5.99:1 in the dark theme (`#8b949e` on `#141414`). The other rules below 4.5:1 have background-like foregrounds (`markup.ignored`, `markup.untracked`, `carriage-return`), which the bundled grammars do not produce. A Shiki update with new theme colors, or a new language, could bring a failing color; the accessibility check in the new tests catches it for the sampled tokens.
- `#656d76` is the color the theme itself uses for muted text, so comments stay in its palette. It is checked against the Fluent background, which is darker than the default theme's `#ffffff`. It also leaves a margin for hosts that set `--codeBlockBackground` to a slightly darker gray, such as Fluent's `colorNeutralBackground3` `#f5f5f5` (4.81:1). Hosts are responsible for the contrast of their own background, as before.
- The default theme also gets `#656d76` for comments. It already passed at 4.55:1, but there is one highlighter for both themes. Existing snapshots are unchanged: the difference is under the image snapshot threshold. The accessibility check in the new tests catches a regression.
- The new test opens the "View code" dialog because axe cannot measure text in the transcript: the transcript focus overlays (`pointer-events: none`) cover it, and axe reports it as "incomplete" instead of failing.
- The code block theme is the `codeBlockTheme` style option and does not follow the color scheme, and the code block background does not follow the Fluent UI theme. So a dark Web Chat can show either code block theme on the same backgrounds as a light one. Verified combinations (lowest token contrast, measured in the transcript and in the "View code" dialog):
   - Default theme, light code theme (`#ffffff`): 5.05:1 (`#8250df`; comments 5.25:1). Dark code theme (`#0d1117`): 6.15:1. The default theme has no dark variant, and `prefers-color-scheme: dark` does not change either background.
   - Fluent theme, light or no Fluent UI theme: light code theme (`#fafafa`) 4.83:1 (`#8250df`; comments 5.03:1), dark code theme (`#141414`) 5.99:1.
   - Fluent theme in a dark Fluent UI theme (`webDarkTheme`): light code theme 4.83:1, dark code theme 5.99:1. The same in the Copilot variant and with a custom brand ramp.
- `markdown/vnext/markdownStreaming.html` keeps its skips: without them, it fails only for the level-one heading (#4721), not for color contrast.

Follow-ups, not in this PR:

- In the dark `side-by-side` pages, the FAQ link in the "View code" dialog is 2.81:1 (`#5661d4`, the test palette's `brand[100]`, on `#292929`). The skip is now limited to the dark theme.
- The accessibility check cannot measure the color contrast of text in the transcript, as described above.

## Specific Changes

- `bundle/src/codeHighlighter/shiki.ts`: the light code block theme (`github-light-default`) replaces the comment color `#6e7781` with `#656d76`
- `component/.../createCodeHighlighterComposer.tsx`: `highlightCode` is optional. Without it, the upstream highlighter is used
- `test/page-object/.../createDirectLineEmulator.js`: the subscribe function is no longer `async`. Its promise was called as a teardown function when Web Chat unmounted, which logged `TypeError: n is not a function`
- Added `__tests__/html2/markdown/codeBlock/contrast.html` (default and Fluent themes, light and dark code themes, and the Fluent theme in a dark Fluent UI theme with either code theme): opens the "View code" dialog for JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python with comments, strings, keywords, and other tokens, with the default accessibility check. Fails on `main` in the Fluent theme, light and dark: `insufficient color contrast of 4.35 (foreground color: #6e7781, background color: #fafafa)`
- Added `__tests__/html2/markdown/codeBlock/remount.html`: renders Web Chat again with the same store and expects the Python code block to be highlighted. Fails on `main` with the code block empty and `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')`
- `__tests__/html2/side-by-side/index.html`: the "View code" dialog step is checked again in the light theme, and the TODO now only mentions the FAQ link in the dark theme

- [x] I have added tests and executed them locally
- [x] I have updated `CHANGELOG.md`
- [ ] I have updated documentation

## Review Checklist

> This section is for contributors to review your work.

- [ ] Accessibility reviewed (tab order, content readability, alt text, color contrast)
- [ ] Browser and platform compatibilities reviewed
- [ ] CSS styles reviewed (minimal rules, no `z-index`)
- [ ] Documents reviewed (docs, samples, live demo)
- [ ] Internationalization reviewed (strings, unit formatting)
- [ ] `package.json` and `package-lock.json` reviewed
- [ ] Security reviewed (no data URIs, check for nonce leak)
- [ ] Tests reviewed (coverage, legitimacy)
